content:
Does Mathlib have code for something like this?

I have a summable function f : a -> b, and a partition c of a (not necessarily into finite parts, and definitely not into finitely many parts); I am looking for a theorem that ensures that the function mapping each part of c to the sum of f on this set is itself summable, with the same sum as f.

I am not 100% clear on the necessary hypotheses on b; at least those required for the use of Summable.subtype (uniformity and completeness), and, I hope, not much more. In my use case b would be a ring of formal power series, and the partition would be into finite parts, most of which have a vanishing sum.
Do you want to allow a partition to be infinitely large?

That seems to be most of it - I don't have a natural candidate for g though.

(Yes, I do need the partition to be into infinitely many parts)
You can set \gamma = Set \beta, and g = return the partition that contains the element
There is also docs#HasSum.sigma with the same flavor.
